chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

The one who preserves his omission and completes it, so there are no two prostrations of omission upon him. Rather, the omission is upon the one who does not know whether he increased or decreased from it.

key_terms.سَهْو: Omission or forgetfulness in ritual acts

ai.seo_question: When are the two prostrations of forgetfulness (Sajd al-Sahw) required in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia juristic distinction between mere forgetfulness and uncertainty (shakk) regarding prayer structure. It establishes that Sajd al-Sahw is not obligatory for those who consciously identify and rectify their error, reserving the prostrations for cases of genuine doubt about whether the prayer was completed correctly. This reflects the principle that ease is preferred when the specific defect is known and corrected.
